verdicts.reason: The finding holds as stated. Every measured base ignores `.devlyn/` in two independent ways. First, the reused materializer appends `.devlyn/` to `.git/info/exclude`. Second, the 4.2.22 installer appends `# devlyn-cli pipeline state` / `.devlyn/` to the project `.gitignore`, and the install commit commits it into the seeded base. rp-d7 m04 actually printed those lines. So no cell ever leaves an untracked `.devlyn/acceptance.json` behind. That is the one state where the helper's clean-tree check (`task-complete.py:426`, "dirty/untracked workspace") pushes a model to edit `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`, so the bookkeeping-commit check (DESIGN.md:137-138, 210-211) never sees the pressure it exists to catch. The check is also commit/PR-scoped by its wording. A `.git/info/exclude` file can never appear in a commit, and no harness check reads it: `transport_state` hashes only `.git/config`. The case is reachable in real use. A `--global` install never touches the project `.gitignore` (devlyn.js:996 calls `readProjectGitignore` only when not global; `updateProjectGitignore` runs only from the project installs at :791/:847), and a remote base may lack the committed rule. ADOPT would ship the note to those users. The design round explicitly flagged this and proposed a guard for a base with neither ignore rule (design-synthesis.json, design-round-grok.md:54). DESIGN r0 dropped that guard (g01–g08 only), and its Interpretation limits (DESIGN.md:217-225) say nothing about it. So the UNSAFE gate (rule 2) would read as covering a case it never exercises. The proposed fix is correct and minimal. It is a disclosure, not a new guard. It improves if it states why the gap matters (the reachable real-world case), so readers do not read the guard pass as safety evidence there.
